title: Count Every Occurrence of a Pattern
statement:
Count how many times `pattern` appears as a block of consecutive letters inside `text`. Occurrences are allowed to **overlap**: in `aaaa` the pattern `aa` appears at positions 0, 1 and 2, which is **3** times.

A slow search compares the pattern with the text at every position and can take `n * m` steps on bad inputs. Aim for time proportional to `n + m`.
constraints: both use only lowercase English letters

examples.explanation: `aba` starts at positions 0, 2 and 4 (the occurrences overlap).

hints.nudge: After a mismatch, do you really have to go back and compare the pattern again from the next text position? What do you already know about the letters you have just matched?
hints.pattern: Knuth-Morris-Pratt: precompute, for every prefix of the pattern, the length of its longest proper prefix that is also a suffix; use it to continue after a mismatch without moving back in the text.
hints.pseudocode:
fail[i] = length of the longest proper prefix of pattern[0..i] that is also a suffix of it
k = 0 (letters matched); count = 0
for each letter ch of the text:
  while k > 0 and ch != pattern[k]: k = fail[k - 1]
  if ch == pattern[k]: k += 1
  if k == len(pattern): count += 1; k = fail[k - 1]
return count
hints.walkthrough: The simple search tries every start position and may re-compare the same text letters many times (for text aaaaaaaaab and pattern aaaaaab it is about n * m steps). KMP never moves backwards in the text. Step 1: for the pattern alone, compute fail[i], the length of the longest prefix of the pattern that is also a suffix of pattern[0..i] (but is shorter than that part). Step 2: scan the text with k = how many pattern letters are currently matched. If the next text letter extends the match, k grows. If not, the pattern letters you matched have a prefix that is also a suffix: instead of starting over, drop to k = fail[k - 1] and try again (repeat until it matches or k is 0). When k reaches the pattern length you found an occurrence; to allow overlaps continue with k = fail[k - 1]. Each text letter makes k grow at most once, and every drop lowers k, so the whole scan is O(n + m).
